arithmetic.do_not_add: the routed-wire and unpriced-capacitance deltas are inside this row already: it simulates the routed netlist against the extracted per-net table, so it prices 100% of the extracted farads. Adding them again double-counts.

glitch_split.internal_is_scaled_not_measured: the internal half is scaled by the signal-transition count, not measured. 2026-10-27-q129-glitch's own limitations: 'the internal-energy term is scaled, not measured ... a glitch on a cell input costs internal energy whether or not the output moves, which this does not price at all.' So the step is part measurement and part scaling, and the scaled share is given here.

board_to_rail_step.residual_is_consistent_with_zero: the fit's residual is 0.142 pJ central, -0.230 on the upper footing, and negative in 12 of 16 configurations on aifoundry3
board_to_rail_step.sram_and_noc_withdrawn: the SRAM and NoC rails are withdrawn as per-MAC switching energies: their whole window delta is their own leakage rise, 66%/61% and 100%/103% of it, so at most 0.13 pJ together and about zero on the central footing

leakage.it_is_not_a_card_constant: a slope rises about 0.009 W/C per C of die temperature on aifoundry2 and about 0.011 on aifoundry3 over 51-65 C, so a correction quoted without its band is ambiguous at the 20-30% level -- larger than the 10% card-to-card difference it is usually invoked for. About three fifths of the gap between E66's 0.2936 and E71's 0.3803 is the temperature band, not the card (69.5% measured the other way round).
leakage.note: not a row. 'Over idle' is already leakage-corrected: E38's registered metric subtracts leak x (t_early - t_launch) from each window, so the window's own die heating is out of the board figure before anything here divides it. What Q129 adds is the slope's band.
leakage.sensitivity_note: E38's registered reduction uses 0.81 / 0.55 W/C; this ledger's own within-run board slope is 0.725 +- 0.019 / 0.358 +- 0.093; E66 measured aifoundry2's IDLE slope at 0.294 W/C over 51-58 C and aifoundry3's idle slope has never been measured, so that row keeps 0.55 for aifoundry3 and is a one-card sensitivity

supersedes: the waterfall of 2026-10-27 (Q128): rail 4.337 pJ carried from E60's per-flipped-bit ratio, bottom-up 1.9465 pJ, unaccounted 3.8365 pJ against the board

transport.the_ceiling_is_violated: one lane's transport model costs 0.654 pJ in the zeros stimulus where the WHOLE BOARD costs 0.27 pJ per multiply-add over idle (E38, per card 0.163 / 0.403 / 0.251), so the 0.4815 pJ register-file row over-prices and a true accounting sits BELOW the bottom of every range here.
transport.why_a_range: the 0.223 pJ its own clock nets cost: whether the lane's register-file clock branches are gated when the card idles decides whether that third of the zero-operand floor is inside the idle E38 subtracts. Unmeasured on silicon.
transport.why_no_glitch_factor: that netlist has no detailed route, no SDF and 37.0% of its capacitance priced, so no glitch factor was measured on it. x1.33 there would be an assumption: it would put the ledger at 4.38-4.68 pJ, 92-98% of the rail, on top of a register-file row the card's own zeros measurement already contradicts.

what: Q129's waterfall for one random fp32 multiply-add, over idle: the board-to-rail step measured instead of carried across, and the bottom-up count rebuilt with routed wires, all of the capacitance, the measured glitch factor and the lane's transport.
what_is_still_unaccounted: 0.58-0.81 pJ against the rail and 0.72-0.94 pJ against the board on the central footing at Miller k=1 (0.04-1.30 and 0.34-1.28 over the whole band), where Q128 had 2.39 and 3.84. Two warnings travel with it. First, the largest single row added here, the lane's transport, carries a register-file model the card's own zeros measurement already contradicts, so the remainder is larger than these numbers say by whatever that model over-prices -- E74 measured a bound on the cell bit (e_cell < 2.73 fJ, 95%) but not the array's own per-MAC energy. Second, the transport netlist is itself a floor on the three axes the arithmetic netlist has now cleared: no detailed route, no glitch measurement, 37.0% of its capacitance priced.
